::: {#sol-why-2012}

Three things changed:

- **Data.**
  AlexNet learned from 1.2 million labelled images [@krizhevsky2012imagenet];
  the zip-code network of 1989 learned from 7,291 digits [@lecun1989backpropagation].
  Datasets grew this way across the field [@goodfellow2016deep, sec. 1.2.2].
- **Computing power.**
  AlexNet was trained on two graphics processing units (GPUs),
  chips built for the arithmetic of drawing images,
  which do many multiplications at once [@krizhevsky2012imagenet].
  Faster hardware let networks grow larger [@goodfellow2016deep, sec. 1.2.3].
- **Techniques.**
  AlexNet used rectified linear units and dropout,
  which made a large network faster to train and less prone to overfitting [@krizhevsky2012imagenet].

The algorithm itself, gradient descent with backpropagation, changed little.

:::
